Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(herein after referred to as Pfa Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of t
he PFA Act and Rules.

2. As per the complaint, on 17.07.2010 at about 1.30 pm, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh. Gian Chand and Sh.
DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra O.P.S Ahlawat under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as LHA)/SDM Sh. Pardeep Baijal visited the premises of M/s R.R. Water, Shop No.
35, LSC Market, Jahangirpuri, New Delhi-110033, where the accused Ashok Kumar Batra was found conducting the business of above said shop where various food articles including packed drinking water bottles bearing identical label declaration.

sentences.text: The Food Inspector disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Packed Drinking Water" from the vendor for analysis.

The sample consisted of 48 sealed pouches of 250 ml each of 'Packaged Drinking Water'
bearing identical label declaration.

The sample was taken under the supervision / direction of Sh Da vs Ashok Kumar Batra on 21 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88767249/
1

entities.text: Sh Da vs Ashok Kumar Batra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Pardeep Baijal SDM/LHA.
The sample was taken as such in originally sealed condition.
The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts so that three sealed bottles constituted one counter part.
Each bottle containing the sample was separately, fastened, marked and sealed according to PFA Act & Rules.
The vendor's signature were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample counter parts.
Notice was given to the accused Ashok Kumar Batra and price of the sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 17.07.2010.
Panchanama was prepared at the spot.
All the documents prepared by FI were signed by the accused Ashok Kumar Batra and the other witness Sh O.P.S Ahlawat, FI.
Before taking sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such Sh O.P.S Ahlawat, FI was joined as witness.

3. One counter-part of the sample was also sent to Public Analyst, DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra Delhi bearing LHA Code number 61/LHA/29278 in intact condition and two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA/SDM in intact condition.

entities.text: Public Analyst, DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the same to be adulterated and misbranded.

The report of the Public Analyst is as follows:-
"The sample is adulterated because aerobic microbial count exceeding the maximum prescribed limit of 100 colonies/ml at 20 deg c to 22 deg c in 72 hrs.
on agar-agar and 20/ml at 37 deg c in 24 hrs.
on agar-agar."
The sample was also misbranded because there was violation of Rule 32(e),(f) and partial violation of rule 32(c)(i).
There was also violation of Rule 42 (zzz) (14) and 49 (28) of PFA Act & Rules.
The Public Analyst also reported regarding label - without declaration of complete address of manufacturer, batch number, date of manufacturing, packaged drinking water and without ISI mark.
4. It is the case of the complainant that accused Ashok Kumar Batra was the Vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s R.R. Water, Shop No. 35, LSC Market, Jahangirpuri, New Delhi-110033 at the time of sampling.

At the time of sampling, accused disclosed that the sampled article of food 'Packaged Drinking Water' was purchased by him from Saurabh but no bill was given by the supplier and that he would provide the bill later.
However, vide letter dated 04.08.2010, accused enclosed a copy of bill No. 372 dated 02.07.2010 issued by M/s. Krishna Industries, Brahmin Mohalla, Near Shiv Mandir, Kheda Kala, Delhi West.
It is stated in the complaint that the two addresses given by the vendor, one at the time of sampling and another given afterwards could not be located despite efforts of Food Inspector.
DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra 5.
Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.
The complaint was then filed in the court on 11.01.2011 alleging violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(e) and (l) of the PFA Act, 1954, punishable under section 7/16(1A) of PFA Act by the accused person.

He also violated section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act and Rule 32(e) (f) and partial violation of Rule 32(c) (i) and also violated the provisions of Rule 42(zzz) (14) and Rule 49(28) of PFA Rules 1955 punishable U/s 16(1)(a) of PFA Act, 1954.

Da vs Ashok Kumar Batra on 21 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88767249/
2 6.
As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 11.01.2011.
No application was moved by accused Ashok Kumar Batra U/s 13 (2) of PFA Act, 1954 to send the second counter-part sample to Director, CFL for analysis.

Based on the report of the PA, notice was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(d) and (m) of the PFA Act, 1954 and for violation of Rule 32(e) (f) and partial violation of Rule 32(c) (i) and violation of provisions of Rule 42(zzz) (14) and Rule 49(28) of PFA Act and Rules and also contravened the provisions of section 2(ix)(k) of PFA Act, punishable U/s 16(1)(a) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
7.

At the trial, the prosecution examined five witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI Sh Gian Chand, PW-2 FI Sh O.P.S Ahlawat, PW3 SDM/LHA Sh. Pardeep Baijal, PW4 Sh. S.N. Bhardwaj, PA DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra and PW5 Ms. Usha Kiran, FI.

entities.text: S.N. Bhardwaj, PA DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW-1 and PW-2 were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Pardeep Baijal.

These witnesses narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 250 ml each of 48 sealed plastic pouches of "Packaged Drinking Water" lying in stitched polythene bags bearing identical label declaration, dividing the sample into three equal parts by taking 16 sealed pouches as such in one counterpart and each counterparts containing the sample, fastened,
marked and sealed and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in form VI Ex. PW-1/B,
Panchnama Ex.PW- 1/C, Notice U/s 14A is Ex.PW1/D, Raid Report Ex.PW1/E. Accused furnished his statement at the spot Ex.PW1/F.

Thereafter, two counterpart of sample along with Memo as per Form-VII were sent to PA for analysis vide PA Receipt Ex. PW- 1/G with the intimation that one counterpart of the same in intact condition has already been deposited with PA Ex.PW1/H.
Thereafter PA Report Ex.PW1/I
was received according to which the sample was found adulterated as well as misbranded.
Letter received from accused through SDM/LHA is Ex.PW1/J alongwith photocopy of bill of purchase of sample commodity Mark X.
During investigation, PW5 sent a letter to VATO, Ward No. 71 regarding constitution of M/s. R.R. Water Ex.PW5/A and in its reply it was stated that no such firm was registered.

Letter sent to Deputy Health Officer, MCD is Ex.PW5/B.
Letter sent to vendor was Ex.PW5/C.
Letter sent to VATO, Ward No. 71 regarding DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra business concern of Mr. Saurabh was Ex.PW5/D.

Letter sent to Deputy Health Officer,
MCD regarding licence of Saurabh is Ex.PW5/E.
Letter sent to Deputy Health Officer,, MCD regarding licence issued to M/s Krishna Industry is Ex.PW5/F. Letter sent to M/s Krishna Industry is Ex.PW5/G.
Letters sent to Mr. Saurabh are Ex.PW5/H and Ex.PW5/H-1.

Reply of Health Officer,
Narela Zone dated 10.11.2010 is Ex.PW5/I.

Thereafter on completion of the investigation, the entire case file alongwith all the documents were sent through LHA/SDM to then Director PFA, who after going through the case file, applied his mind and gave his consent for prosecution Ex.PW3/A.
Thereafter, the present complaint Ex.PW2/A was filed before this Court.
Then intimation letter Ex.PW2/B alongwith copies of PA's Report were sent to the accused through registered post.
All the witnesses were duly cross examined by the Ld Defence Counsel.
During cross- examination, PW1 stated that the word 'Packaged Drinking Water' was not mentioned on the pouches.

He denied the suggestion that accused wrote the words on Notice in Form VI "These pouches are of same lot"
under his dictation and threat and added that accused had written them voluntarily.

PW2 admitted Da vs Ashok Kumar Batra on 21 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88767249/
3 during his cross-examination that photocopy of bill dated 02.07.2010 was received by FI Gian Chand after lifting the sample and added that it was not in his knowledge that one Saurabh Kumar Mahajan, the alleged supplier of sample commodity had sent a letter to Director, PFA Mark DA.
He further admitted that accused had disclosed the source of purchase of sample commodity by making an endorsement on Notice under Form VI.

He further admitted that if he lot number was not mentioned on the sealed packet of sample commodity, then only DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra the manufacturer knew whether they were of same lot or different lot.
He added that during investigation, manufacturer could not be traced and therefore, he was not impleaded as an accused in the case.
PW5 stated during her cross-examination that she was not aware if two letters dated 30.07.2010 was sent by Saurabh Kumar Mahajan to Director, PFA Mark DX-1 and Mark DX-2.

She stated that she was also not aware of bill Mark DX-3.
8.
Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was recorded on 20.02.2018 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.
He stated that the sample was purchased from Krishna Industries and original bill was placed on record.
Thereafter the matter was fixed for defence evidence.
9. In his defence, the accused Ashok Kumar Batra examined himself as DW-1.
As DW1, the accused stated that he had purchased the sample commodity from Krishna Industries whose proprietor was Saurabh Majahan.
The katcha bill was Ex.DW1/A which was shown to the FI who refused to accept the same.

He added that supplier Saurabh Mahajan refused to give pakka bill and so he filed a complaint Ex.DW1/B before PS Mahindra Park and on interference with police, the supplier issued pakka bill Mark DX-3.
During his cross-examination by Ld. SPP for complainant
, he stated that the bill Mark DX-3 was prepared in PS by Saurabh Mahajan and admitted that the bill is dated 02.07.2010.
He denied that Mark DX3 and Mark DW1/1 were forged and fabricated.

Thereafter,
defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra 10.
In a criminal trial, the burden is on the complainant / prosecution to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
This burden cannot be shifted to the accused and has to be necessarily discharged by the prosecution itself by leading cogent and trustworthy evidence.
However, if the accused has any defence, then the burden to prove that defence lies upon the accused.
11.The present case is for adulteration and misbranding of food article i.e. Packaged Drinking Water.
12. Admittedly, as per the judicial record the accused is not the manufacturer of the sampled commodity 'Packaged Drinking Water'.
This fact has also not been disputed or denied by the concerned Food Officials themselves.

In fact, PW2 has himself admitted that the accused had disclosed the name of manufacturer and only for the reason that the manufacturer could not be traced, he was not made an accused in the present case.
Perusal of letter Mark DX1 reflects that Saurabh Kumar Mahajan had admitted supplying the sampled food article to accused.
The said letter is dated 30.07.2010.
The bill Mark DX- 3 is dated 02.07.2010.

The sample was lifted by the Da vs Ashok Kumar Batra on 21 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88767249/
4 concerned Food Officials on 17.07.2010.
Therefore, it is seen that the bill pertains to the same period.
It was in the knowledge of the concerned Food Officials at all times that the accused Ashok Kumar Batra was not the manufacturer of the sample commodity.
Merely, the fact that the Saurabh Kumar Mahajan could not be traced is not the reason for not impleading him as an accused.

The food officials during their cross-examination at the time of DA vs Ashok Kumar Batra their deposition have also not denied the bill dated 02.07.2010 and the letter of Saurabh Kumar Mahajan dated 30.07.2010, but have only stated that they were not aware.
It appears therefore, in view of the aforesaid discussions that the manufacturer was intentionally not arrayed as an accused in the present case.

The sample food article 'Packaged Drinking Water' was found intact in sealed pouches at the time of sampling and there is nothing on record which suggests any tempering on the part of the accused/vendor Ashok Kumar Batra.
There is nothing on record which imputes any violation as alleged on his part as it has been proved that he was only a vendor.

13. In view of the aforesaid facts, benefit is given to the accused in the present case as charges of adulteration and misbranding qua the sampled food commodity 'Packaged Drinking Water' are not proved against the accused.
14. Accordingly, accused Ashok Kumar Batra is hereby acquitted of all charges framed against him in the present case.

15. Ordered accordingly.
Announced in the open court on 21.05.2019 (Gurmohina Kaur)
